title: architecture-review-kv-cache-splitter-followup-2026-05-12
content:
Architecture review follow-up: KV cache splitter design
Date: 2026-05-12
Attendees: Ava Martinez (notes), Ravi Patel, Chen Li, Sofia Gomez, Marcus Brown, Emily Zhao (observer)
Location: Zoom / #eng-serving-runtime

Agenda:
- Quick recap of RFC-142 decisions and open questions
- Present splitter prototype behavior and benchmarks
- Discuss multi-tenant routing implications and fallback behavior
- Eviction and prefetch interactions with splitter
- Action items and owners

Recap / context:
- RFC-142 approved core sharding approach: deterministic shard mapping based on request fingerprint, with routing fallback to compatible model variants.
- Open concerns from previous review: splitter complexity, cross-shard requests, cache hotkeys, and eviction interplay.

Prototype summary (Chen):
- Implemented a ‘splitter’ layer that maps a request fingerprint to one or more KV cache shards based on a tunable fanout. Default fanout=1, can increase to 2-3 for redundancy/hotkey smoothing.
- Benchmarks on m60 cluster: fanout=1 median p50 token latency unchanged, fanout=2 +5% latency; hit-rate improved 12% for synthetic hotkey workloads.
- Memory overhead per shard: small (metadata + index), roughly +1.8% per extra replica.
- Prototype supports atomic reservation for in-flight KV writes to avoid double-populate races.

Key discussion points and decisions:
1) Fanout default and knobs:
   - Decision: keep default fanout=1 for most customers to minimize latency and memory. Expose fanout as a per-route config for customers hitting hotkey issues.
   - Rationale: most workloads don’t have extreme hotkeys; fewer injections of redundancy lowers tail latency and cost.

2) Multi-tenant routing and isolation:
   - Concern: splitter could route fragments for a single logical request across shards with different tenant placement, causing cross-tenant resource hotspots and complexity for Private deployments.
   - Decision: enforce tenant-affinity constraint in splitter. A split is only allowed across shards that have the same tenant isolation level or are in the same placement group. Splitter will consult placement metadata service.
   - Follow-up: platform-engineering to provide placement API for quick lookup (see action items).

3) Cross-shard read/write consistency and in-flight writes:
   - Approach: use write-through for cache populates; when fanout>1 we perform parallel writes and use lightweight per-key locks to avoid double-runner generation. If a write fails on secondary shard, system continues with best-effort and emits metric SRV.cache.write_failures.
   - Decision: accept best-effort secondary writes for now but add metrics and alerting. Revisit if failure rate >0.5%.

4) Eviction policy interplay:
   - Issue: duplicated entries across shards inflate resident set and make eviction less effective.
   - Proposal: maintain per-key replica-count metadata and make eviction LRU-aware across replicas (evict lowest value keys across all replicas first).
   - Decision: defer complex cross-shard coordinated eviction for next quarter. Implement a simpler heuristic: when fanout>1, treat replicas as lower-priority for eviction until population stabilizes. Add a telemetry flag to measure waste-resident-memory.

5) Prefetch / cache warming interaction:
   - Note: current prefetch engine assumes single-shard mapping; with fanout>1, it should prefer replicas that minimize cross-device traffic.
   - Action: Sofia to prototype prefetch affinity logic that prefers local shard replicas.

6) Metrics and observability:
   - New metrics agreed: SRV.cache.splitter.fanout, SRV.cache.splitter.hit_rate_by_fanout, SRV.cache.splitter.write_failures, SRV.cache.splitter.replica_memory_overhead, SRV.cache.splitter.cross_shard_traffic
   - Dashboard: add a per-route pane showing fanout, hit rate, and tail latency. Marcus to add to Redwood Console mockups.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- How does splitter interact with model-variant fallback routing during capacity pressure? Example: original shard may be on variant A, fallback routed to variant B with different KV layout. Need explicit compatibility rules. Action: Ravi to draft compatibility matrix and update RFC-142 appendix.
- Operational complexity for Private deployments where shard placement is fixed. Need tighter admin controls in Private control plane.
- Cost impact analysis: estimated +1.8% memory per replica, but the real cost depends on working set; Finance wants a rough order-of-magnitude. Action: Chen to produce a short cost model by 2026-05-20.

Action items (owners + approx ETA):
- Platform-engineering: expose placement metadata API for splitter (ETA 2026-05-26) - owner: Marcus Brown
- Draft compatibility matrix for model-variant + shard mapping (ETA 2026-05-18) - owner: Ravi Patel
- Prefetch affinity prototype (ETA 2026-05-24) - owner: Sofia Gomez
- Cost model for replica overhead (ETA 2026-05-20) - owner: Chen Li
- Add splitter metrics and Console mockups (ETA 2026-05-28) - owner: Marcus Brown
- Add alert SRV.cache.write_failures and create runbook stub (ETA 2026-05-22) - owner: Ava Martinez

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Keep default fanout=1 to reduce blast radius. Allow customers to opt into higher fanout via per-route policy with cost warnings.
- Re-evaluate eviction design after data from telemetry (2-3 weeks of production-ish traffic).
- Consider a lightweight global replica index service if cross-replica coordination proves necessary; this is higher risk/infra cost and should be shelved unless telemetry indicates >5% wasted memory due to duplicates.

Meeting wrap-up:
- Overall consensus: splitter is promising for hotkey smoothing and redundancy, but feature should be opt-in with conservative defaults. We prioritized observability, tenant-affinity, and metrics before wide rollout.
- Next sync: short async update in #eng-serving-runtime in one week; schedule follow-up architecture review if any action item slips or cost/compatibility reveals issues.

Attachments / links used in discussion:
- RFC-142-kv-cache-sharding (arch doc)
- GH-PR-2385-kv-splitter-proto (prototype code)
- JIRA-SRV-1124 (splitter epic)

Raw notes / side conversations (informal):
- Ravi: "If we get too clever with cross-shard eviction we will have 5x the complexity for little gain"
- Chen: "Bench numbers are synthetic; need to run on real traffic to validate p99 impact"
- Sofia: "Prefetch affinity seems low-risk — could give a lot of benefit for chat workloads with sticky prefixes"

Status: draft notes, please comment inline or ping Ava for corrections.
